text:
Edmonton scored five goals in a second period where it generated 1.29 expected goals, and one of them, Evan Bouchard's slap shot 11 seconds into the frame, came on a chance the model rated at under 1%. That goal cut ANA's lead to 2-1 and started the run. Kasperi Kapanen tied it on the power play at 6:30, Bouchard added another slap shot at 14:12, and Vasily Podkolzin and Connor McDavid finished it in the final three-plus minutes. Leon Draisaitl assisted on four of the five.

Anaheim had controlled the opening 20 minutes, outchancing EDM 1.57 to 0.87 in expected goals, and Beckett Sennecke scored twice on the power play, at 4:11 and 15:28, to make it 2-0. Over the whole game, ANA held a 74-43 edge in shot attempts and 31-19 in shots on goal, and the simulated replays of every shot give ANA a 59% chance of winning to EDM's 41%. Sennecke put up seven shots on goal and skated 25:00.

The gap between play and result came down to goaltending. Lukas Dostal allowed 5 goals on 17 shots against an expected 2.15, about 2.9 goals worse than the chances he faced deserved, and Ville Husso stopped both shots he saw in relief. Devon Levi stopped 29 of 31 for EDM, 1.2 goals better than expected. ANA also had 3.20 expected goals to EDM's 2.69, and still lost 5-2.
